official siteplaybuild articleplayer reportindependent post

The complete rule set is visible before the ride

Assignment: the first sleepy American street contains 40 houses and 10 subscribers, with raised mailbox flags identifying targets on both sides. The bike pedals itself; the player chooses line, speed, and throw timing.

Controls: left/right steer between pavements, up/down sprint or brake, Space delivers, the mouse aims, and X smashes a paper at windows, hazards, or the dog. Touch controls map the same verbs to dragging, tapping, and a second finger.

Scoring and survival: a clean delivery adds 100 points, the streak multiplier reaches ×5, a perfect morning pays 2,500 points and adds a subscriber, and a crash removes one of three lives. Missing a subscriber cancels them. Losing all lives or all subscribers ends the week.

Escalation: Monday through Sunday promises wider streets, trickier turns, a growing round, rush hour, a long haul, and the big run. More traffic appears each morning; grades range S/A/B/C and the best ten weeks feed the leaderboard.

Hazards taught on screen

  • Dogs notice the rider at 30m
  • Papers can distract or stop the dog
  • Potholes, kids, cars, and poor lines cost momentum
  • Radar shows target side and approach distance
  • Subscribers function as week health
  • Front-page results are designed to be shared

Recorded performance makes learning visible

00:00–01:04

The page explains assignment, controls, seven-day progression, scoring, leaderboard, privacy, and the Astra/Blender build. Before playing, the user must provide an email and X username; handle, scores, times, grades, and days are public while email is private.

01:04–03:20

The first ride establishes the moving HUD and hazards. One clean delivery is followed by collisions and misses. The result is 1/10, 300 points, 0:43, grade C. Nine missed subscribers remove the entire audience, ending the week.

03:20–06:53

A second attempt uses the park line, ramps, targets, and better pacing. It reaches 5/10, 2,098 points, 1:03, grade B, plus a 148-point speed bonus. Five subscribers survive, so the route can continue to the next day.

Strong · rules match live feedback

The pre-game explanation names exactly what the HUD later shows: mailbox side, distance, papers, lives, subscribers, streak, and timing window. The player can connect a miss to the weekly consequence.

Strong · failure preserves a learnable score

The first C and second B create a clear improvement story within seven minutes. Delivery count, time, speed bonus, grade, and subscriber loss each explain a different dimension.

Friction · registration precedes proof

Email and X username are mandatory before the first moving street. That trades a potentially high share/leaderboard identity for a large first-session abandonment risk.

Friction · 10 subscribers can collapse instantly

One weak opening street removes all nine missed households and ends the whole week. The consequence is coherent, but the first attempt offers no buffer for learning aim and traffic together.

Recommendations

Offer a guest first ride

Let the player complete one local run, then request registration to preserve the week, publish a result, or enter the leaderboard.

Protect the first three subscribers

Use a short practice block or temporary insurance before the full 10-house route, then apply normal churn once aim and braking are demonstrated.

Turn misses into one actionable replay

On results, mark early/late/wrong-side/crash misses and replay the worst delivery window. The grade should teach the next attempt, not only label it.

Screen-by-screen product anatomy

Interface specification

A reconstruction-oriented inventory of the visible hierarchy, controls, states, interruptions, and feedback in PaperRoute. It describes observed recording evidence first; recommendations are explicitly labelled.

Evidence convention. Observed means the state is visible in the reviewed session or captured UI. Implementation guidance marks a production requirement inferred from the interaction model, not a claim about unseen code.

Viewport map

Moving street canvas

The road scrolls through the center with the bicycle low/center and subscriber houses on both sides. Mailboxes, hazards, windows, dogs, and aim path occupy the action field.

Delivery HUD

Points, speed, clock, radar/distance, lives, delivered/subscriber count, paper ammo, and streak frame the canvas without obscuring the upcoming delivery lane.

Assignment and results

Pre-run newspaper briefing, control/tutorial page, evening newspaper results, leaderboard, share, retry, and continue use readable editorial panels outside the high-speed scene.

Overlays & interruptions

  • Morning newspaper assignment and device-specific control tutorial.
  • Pause/settings/help layer that freezes the moving street.
  • Crash/recovery state in the canvas, distinct from the route-ending result.
  • Evening newspaper with grade, bonuses, subscriber changes, leaderboard/share, Retry, and Continue.

Motion, VFX & feedback

  • Paper follows a readable ballistic arc; mailbox hit creates sparkle, signed score, and streak travel to HUD.
  • Smash hit uses window shards and a stronger sound; misses and wrong targets get distinct feedback.
  • Bike lean, wheel speed, road parallax, sprint/brake treatment, and camera motion communicate velocity.
  • Dog chase and collision use anticipation, impact shake, life loss, and temporary recovery indication.
  • Result grade and speed bonus count up only after the route freezes, so the player can audit the total.

Responsive, accessibility & edge cases

  • Honor the documented touch scheme and landscape layout with sufficiently large aim/steer areas and no browser-gesture conflicts.
  • Offer camera shake/flash reduction, remappable keys, and aim sensitivity; high speed amplifies discomfort and precision problems.
  • Subscriber state needs flag shape/label as well as color; audio cues should have visual equivalents.
  • Pause on visibility loss and save only at route boundaries to prevent duplicated grade/subscriber changes.
Reconstruction test. A player should read the assignment, operate with keyboard/mouse or touch, identify the delivery window, score a normal and smash throw, build and lose a streak, survive or understand a crash, finish the route, audit the grade/bonus, and know exactly how the subscriber list changed.

Creator context · verified public sources

Developer dossier

Who made PaperRoute, the public context around the work, and the nearest verified projects. Private identity, location, employment, and credits are left unknown unless the creator or an official project page states them.

Public identity and credit

PaperRoute is publicly credited to Emm Tee / Built by Sketch. The official build notes say it was made with Graft by BuiltBySketch plus GPT Astra and Blender, connecting the product, maker identity, and tools without implying that an AI system is the legal author.

Location and working context

The public @builtbysketch profile lists London, United Kingdom. It describes the creator as working on AI-era startups/products and building DevClocked, with a previous agency exit and recommerce experience.

Timeline

PaperRoute was publicly documented in September 2026. Its own build page reports roughly 35 hours, 1.51 billion tokens, and 69 checkpoints; those are project-reported production metrics and remain labelled as such rather than converted into conventional team-hours.

Other verified work

The clearly linked current product is DevClocked. The developer has also shared an internal football physics engine for a football-manager concept; that is best described as ongoing prototype work, not a separately verified shipped game.

Visible development pattern

The project demonstrates an explicitly documented AI-assisted production workflow wrapped around a highly authored 1980s paper-delivery game structure. Public communication emphasizes process transparency, rapid iteration, checkpoints, and shareable results.

What this means for the teardown

For reconstruction, separate the reproducible game rules and screen system from the reported tooling statistics. The build log is useful process evidence, but it does not reveal prompts, source ownership, final asset provenance, or the cost/quality of recreating the result with another stack.

Identity boundary. Emm Tee is a public display name and Built by Sketch the public maker identity. Location and work claims are profile-provided; prototype mentions are not upgraded to released products without an official release page.

04
Reconstruction blueprint

What must exist to rebuild the observed game

This is a product and systems specification derived from the public build and the recorded first session. It describes observable behaviour, not the original source-code architecture.

Reconstruction confidence. High for registration, assignment, controls, delivery scoring, hazards, subscriber/life loss, grades, and two Monday attempts. Medium for Tuesday–Sunday escalation and the full public leaderboard/retention loop.

State machineSession flow

  • Identity gate → register email and X handle before entering the public score system.
  • Morning assignment → receive forty houses, ten subscribers, three lives, raised-flag targeting, and route rules.
  • Auto-forward run → steer, sprint/brake, aim left/right, throw papers, and react to hazards and radar.
  • Delivery resolution → clean hit, miss, smash, distraction, streak, and speed bonuses update score/state.
  • Route result → grade the morning, remove missed subscribers, preserve survivors, and decide whether the week continues.
  • Week state → advance Monday through Sunday with escalation, or end when all subscribers/lives are lost.

Input contractControls

  • The bicycle moves automatically; Left/Right steer and Up/Down sprint or brake.
  • Space delivers a paper; mouse aiming chooses the throw direction/side.
  • X performs a smash action against windows, hazards, or the dog where applicable.
  • Touch equivalents are documented on the instruction screen.

Rules engineSimulation and resolution

  • The first assignment contains forty houses but only ten subscribers, identified by raised flags on both sides.
  • A clean delivery awards 100 points and supports a streak multiplier that can reach ×5.
  • A perfect morning awards 2,500 and a new subscriber.
  • Missing a subscriber cancels that subscriber; losing all subscribers or all three lives ends the week.
  • The dog detects the rider at 30 m; thrown papers can distract it.
  • Radar previews upcoming side and distance, while children, potholes, cars, dogs, and street geometry compete for attention.
  • Grades S/A/B/C summarise performance; speed adds a separate end-of-run bonus.

Meta layerEconomy and progression

  • The campaign escalates from Monday through Sunday rather than resetting every attempt into an isolated score.
  • Subscribers act as both targets and persistent health: misses shrink the next day's audience.
  • The first run scored 300, delivered 1/10, earned C, and lost the week after nine misses.
  • The second run delivered 5/10, scored 2,098 in 1:03, earned B with a 148 speed bonus, and retained five subscribers.
  • Public handle, scores, times, grades, and days are visible; email is declared private, but registration is mandatory and unverified.

Required screen and interface inventory

Email/X registration and privacy copy
Morning assignment with houses, subscribers, lives, flags, and side rules
Keyboard/mouse and touch instructions
Auto-forward street HUD with score, streak, lives, papers, timer, and radar
Subscriber flag and clean-delivery feedback
Dog detection/distraction and street hazards
Missed-house/subscriber feedback
Morning result with deliveries, score, time, speed bonus, and grade
Subscriber-loss / week-continuation or week-over state
Public score/identity surface

Minimum useful data model

  • RouteDefinition: ordered road spline, forty house slots, subscriber flags/sides, hazards, speed zones, spawn seed.
  • RiderState: lateral position, forward speed, lives, papers, aim side/angle, active stun/crash state.
  • DeliveryEvent: target house, throw trajectory, hit quality, clean/miss/smash, base score, streak result.
  • HazardDefinition: trigger volume, warning range, collision effect, dog aggro radius and distraction response.
  • WeekState: day, subscribers, lives, cumulative grades/scores, unlocked difficulty, terminal reason.
  • PublicProfile: handle, visible score/time/grade/day fields, private email, consent/version, moderation status.

06
Production sequence

Build the causal loop before the content surface

A practical implementation order for reproducing the observed promise while keeping the prototype testable at every step.

  1. Build an auto-forward road with lateral steering, speed control, left/right throw trajectories, and ten flagged targets.
  2. Add clean-hit detection, 100-point scoring, streaks, misses, subscriber removal, three lives, and a result grade.
  3. Add radar telegraphing and one example each of pothole, car, child, and 30 m dog/distraction behaviour.
  4. Expand to forty houses and a seven-day state with escalation, perfect bonus, new subscribers, and week failure.
  5. Add guest play before identity; then implement opt-in accounts, privacy, public boards, validation, and anti-cheat.

Boundaries and unresolved behaviour

Do not encode these as facts yet.
  • Tuesday–Sunday content, escalation curves, route variation, and a successful complete week were not recorded.
  • Exact throw physics, clean-hit thresholds, streak reset rules, grade thresholds, and every hazard penalty need instrumentation.
  • The public leaderboard lifecycle, identity verification, moderation, deletion, and privacy operations were not tested.

Metric discipline

Creator-reported plays, users, registrations, page views, reactions, and live counters preserve their original labels. They are not combined into one audience total or treated as retention.

Reading rule. Statements in the teardown describe what the reviewed evidence supports. Items in “Boundaries and unresolved behaviour” are explicit follow-up questions for deeper capture or implementation research.
